name: The Gülhane London Plane
verified_sources: https://services5.arcgis.com/26ObnytmBZ58Wbj8/arcgis/rest/services/turkiye_anit_agaclari/FeatureServer/0/query?where=OBJECTID=398&outFields=*&f=json (Turkiye Anit Agaclari national monumental-tree registry, OBJECTID 398)

https://www.konusanagac.com/ozel-agac/83/londra-cinari-gulhane-parki-platanus-acerifolia.html (Istanbul Metropolitan Municipality Parks, Gardens and Green Areas Dept., 'Konusan Agaclar' individually-named-tree project)
access: Free, inside Gulhane Park (open daily, standard park hours, no ticket)
transport: Gulhane tram stop (T1 line) at the park's Sarayburnu-side gate, immediate walk
verify_notes: Two official sources agree closely: the national ArcGIS registry (turkiye_anit_agaclari, OBJECTID 398) records height 33m, trunk diameter 170cm, age 277 years; IBB's own Konusan Agaclar municipal project publishes a dedicated page for this exact tree with the identical 33m/170cm figures and states it has stood in Gulhane Park 'since 1741'. 1741 + 277 = 2018, so both figures trace to the same circa-2018 survey rather than being fully independent re-measurements; still two separately published official sources (national registry + Istanbul Metropolitan Municipality) agreeing on species, size and location, which is stronger than either alone. Adding roughly 8 years since that survey gives ~285 today. Flagged rather than clean-confirmed only because I could not find a fully independent (non-shared-survey) third source in this pass. Species caution: the registry's Turkish-name-to-Latin pairing 'Londra Cinari/Platanus acerifolia' has been shown elsewhere in this city's own data (ist_001, ist_002) to be misapplied to Oriental Planes far too old to be the London Plane hybrid (which only originated c.1670, capping a real specimen near 350 years). This tree's age of roughly 285 years is well within that cap, so the London Plane identification is plausible here, unlike those older cases; not proven by a photo or independent botanical ID, so keep flagged. Part of a genuine walkable cluster: sits about 550m from the already-published Taslı Cinar (ist_004) and about 350m from the Topkapi Palace Courtyard Plane (ist_011), all inside Gulhane Park/Topkapi grounds.

name: The Gülhane Nettle Tree
verified_sources: https://services5.arcgis.com/26ObnytmBZ58Wbj8/arcgis/rest/services/turkiye_anit_agaclari/FeatureServer/0/query?where=OBJECTID=400&outFields=*&f=json (Turkiye Anit Agaclari national monumental-tree registry, OBJECTID 400)

https://www.konusanagac.com/ozel-agac/81/citlenbik-gulhane-parki-celtis-australis.html (Istanbul Metropolitan Municipality Parks, Gardens and Green Areas Dept., 'Konusan Agaclar' individually-named-tree project)
access: Free, inside Gulhane Park (open daily, standard park hours, no ticket)
transport: Gulhane tram stop (T1 line) at the park's Sarayburnu-side gate, short walk within the park
verify_notes: Same corroboration pattern as ist_012, about 40m away in the same park: the national registry (OBJECTID 400) records height 23m, trunk diameter 145cm, age 259 years; IBB's Konusan Agaclar project publishes a dedicated page for this specific tree with matching 23m/145cm figures and says it has stood in Gulhane Park 'since 1759'. 1759 + 259 = 2018, again pointing to a shared circa-2018 survey rather than two fully independent field measurements, so flagged for that reason even though the two sources do not conflict. Adding roughly 8 years gives ~265-267 today. Celtis australis (nettle/hackberry) is a genuinely long-lived, sturdy species in Mediterranean/Anatolian settings, so an age in the 250-300 year range is physically plausible, unlike some of the registry's plane-tree age claims elsewhere. Third of the walkable Gulhane cluster: roughly 40m from ist_012 (Gulhane London Plane), about 500m from the Taslı Cinar (ist_004), about 300m from the Topkapi Palace Courtyard Plane (ist_011).

name: The Topkapı Palace Yew

location.address: Topkapı Palace, Fourth Courtyard area, Cankurtaran, Fatih, Istanbul

verified_sources: https://services5.arcgis.com/26ObnytmBZ58Wbj8/arcgis/rest/services/turkiye_anit_agaclari/FeatureServer/0/query?where=OBJECTID=141&outFields=*&f=json (Turkiye Anit Agaclari national monumental-tree registry, OBJECTID 141: Porsuk/Taxus baccata, 314 yrs, govde_capi 103cm, boy 13m, tepe_capi 12m)

https://www.monumentaltrees.com/en/tur/marmararegion/istanbul/2138_topkapipalace/ (independent crowdsourced database; lists exactly 3 European Yew (Taxus baccata) specimens individually measured in Topkapi Palace's 4th courtyard, girths 3.26m and 3.09m at 1.30m plus one unmeasured, photos dated 6 December 2014)
access: Paid entry (Topkapi Palace Museum ticket covers the inner courtyards, including the 4th courtyard/Tulip Garden area)
transport: Gulhane tram stop (T1 line), then roughly 10-15 minute walk through the palace grounds to the 4th courtyard
verify_notes: Species and general location (Topkapi Palace's 4th courtyard) are corroborated by two genuinely separate sources: Turkiye's national monumental-tree registry (OBJECTID 141, individually surveyed coordinates, age 314 years, trunk diameter 103cm, crown 12m, height 13m) and monumentaltrees.com's independent field survey, which lists exactly 3 European Yew specimens in that same courtyard with their own girth measurements (3.26m and 3.09m circumference at breast height, matching a trunk in the 100+cm-diameter range) and dated photos from December 2014, confirming they were alive and standing then. The registry's own detail page (anitagaclar.gov.tr/detail/porsuk--taxus-baccata/112, same underlying government database as the ArcGIS layer so not counted as a second independent source) repeats the same trunk/crown/height figures almost exactly but gives age as 310 rather than 314, a minor internal drift between two views of the same record, and lists the district as 'GOLBASI' rather than Fatih, which is a clear data-entry error since its own descriptive text is explicitly about Topkapi Sarayi; flagging this as a register data-quality issue worth knowing about rather than a location problem, since the coordinates and the prose both independently point at Topkapi. Picked the oldest (314yr) of the three registered yews in this courtyard as the entry; the other two (OBJECTIDs 403, 404) are close by and go to leads rather than being folded in, since they read as separate individual specimens rather than one visitor-facing point. Not clean-confirmed because the most recent direct alive-evidence found this pass (monumentaltrees photos) dates to 2014, about 12 years old; no fresher sighting found in this pass. Fourth stop in the Topkapi/Gulhane cluster: about 550m from ist_012/ist_013 in Gulhane Park, inside the same palace grounds as the already-published Topkapi Palace Courtyard Plane (ist_011).
